start_here: Say to your AI: "Add a 15 minute task called Water the sample ferns to my calendar tasks, then show me my calendar tasks." It calls the calendar page route twice, a POST to /calendar/tasks and a GET, and reads the task back from your own records.

lists.label: Calendar
lists.holds: Meetings and time blocks: when each starts and ends, who comes and where it happens; the page's calendar names it as a source this route's run cannot read, and says so in its own words.

instructions: 1. Pour the example tasks into the task list you already keep (see pour), or let the first call make list:calendar-tasks for you: a read makes the calendar's starting lists once when they are missing and keeps no task.

2. Say what you want done on the calendar; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:answer-the-calendar-page-route and input {path, method, query, body}: GET /calendar reads the sources, GET and POST /calendar/tasks read and change tasks (action create, schedule, complete and the others the owner knows).

3. Read the answer {status, body}: 200 with the owner's body (the task and an undo for a create, the tasks list for a read), or the owner's refusal in its words with its status; every write is conditional on what was read, so a record changed meanwhile is never written over.
4. /calendar/actions and /calendar/availability answer 404 here; sources only another route or a connected calendar tool can read (meetings, posts) are said unread in the calendar's own words.

worked_examples.title: Add a 15 minute task, then read the tasks back
worked_examples.ask: Add a 15 minute task called Water the sample ferns to my calendar, then list my tasks.
worked_examples.given: From tools/keep-my-calendar-in-my-accounts-own-records-with-its-lists-files/test/calendar-route.test.mjs (the same first test): the account has no calendar tasks yet. The answer below was produced by running src/calendar-route.mjs against that test's in-memory records door.
worked_examples.hands_back: {status: 200, body: {task: {id: "calendar-fern-1", title: "Water the sample ferns", duration_minutes: 15, status: "To do", description: "", labels: [], priority: null, due: null, starts_at: null, ends_at: null, may_move: true, may_cancel: false, created_at: <the time of the run>, ...}, kept: false, undo: {action: "restore", rows: [{task_id: "calendar-fern-1", remove: true}]}}}; the record record:calendar-task:calendar-fern-1 is kept and list:calendar-tasks is made once. A following GET /calendar/tasks answers {status: 200, body: {list_id: "calendar-tasks", tasks: [that task], collections: [], page: {complete: true, next_cursor: null}, ...}}. POST /calendar/availability answers {status: 404, body: {error: "Not found"}}.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
